title: When Should a Call Centre Reallocate Staff After a Demand Shock?
grain: One queued telephone call between 08:00 and 13:00 on a Sunday–Thursday business day
dataset: Technion Service Engineering Israeli bank call-centre logs
question: When, within a fixed staffing budget, should a manager release temporary service capacity?
design: Estimate censored patience and service by call type from January–July. Select base staffing against both waiting and abandonment in August–September. Replay October–December arrivals under fixed, queue-triggered and receding-horizon dispatch. Calls already in service continue after a flexible staffing interval ends.
boundary: Historical outcomes describe observed calls. Staffing schedules, patience past the censoring point, operator flexibility and policy-dependent waits are simulated. The five-hour morning replay begins with an empty queue.
redistribution: Prepared extract removes customer and employee identifiers. Original research data and documentation remain available at the Technion.

fields.call: Date, telephone line and source call number
fields.served: 1 when served, 0 when the caller abandoned
fields.service: Observed service duration in seconds; blank for abandoned calls
